title: Floor Walk Before Audit
brief: Meridian Microworks has its certification audit in 10 days. You walk the wafer polishing floor, from incoming inspection to pack and ship, as an internal auditor. You have 12 visit points. Cover the whole floor.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Carrier labels at the clean station
Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Technician: what to do after a particle alarm
Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Chemical acceptance records: each of 9 lots this month has a certificate of analysis compared with the specification and signed.
Work instruction at polisher P-4 is revision F; the document system shows revision G released 3 weeks ago with a new pad-change interval.
evidence.whyItMatters: Current approved instructions must be at the point of use.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare revision letters with the document system.

evidence.text: Thickness gauge TG-2 calibration label expired 9 days ago; the log shows it measured 6 lots since then.
evidence.whyItMatters: Measurements from an instrument past calibration cannot be relied on; earlier results need review.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read due dates on every gauge in use.

evidence.text: Particle monitor alarm log shows 3 alarms in bay 2 last week with no response entries.
evidence.whyItMatters: The environment for operations must be maintained, and excursions responded to and recorded.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read alarm logs for response entries.

evidence.text: 2 carriers at final clean carry hand-written lot numbers L-883 and L-883B with no record of a lot split in the system.
evidence.whyItMatters: Lot identity must be maintained through every split.

evidence.text: Customer wafers for 2 customers are staged together on shelf S-4 without separation labels.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer property must be identified and kept separate.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check staging shelves for mixed ownership.

evidence.text: Qualification matrix is current; all 22 technicians are qualified for their stations.
Technician: "After an alarm we wait and see if it clears. I'm not sure if we should record it." Procedure CR-5 requires a record.
evidence.whyItMatters: Awareness of the procedure is weak; strengthening it would close the gap seen in the alarm log.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask staff what they do after an alarm.

evidence.text: Quarantine shelf holds 1 rejected chemical lot with a tag and disposition pending.
Gowning area mirror is cracked at the corner.
evidence.whyItMatters: A cracked mirror is a facilities matter; gowning follows the posted steps.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The mirror does not affect the process.

evidence.text: Outgoing inspection records for the last 10 shipments are complete and signed.
Carriers use different colors by product family, as allowed by the handling instruction.
evidence.whyItMatters: Color coding supports identification and is defined.

decisions.prompt: Which finding needs action today rather than in the report?
options: The overdue gauge TG-2 and the mixed customer wafers on shelf S-4, because product may ship on unreliable measurements or to the wrong customer
decisions.rationale: Issues that can affect product or customers now come first.

containment: Withdraw gauge TG-2 and review the 6 lots measured; separate and label wafers on shelf S-4
correction: Replace revision F with G at P-4, record the lot split, and record responses to the 3 alarms
cause: Floor controls depend on memory: no due-date alert, no staging rule, and no alarm response prompt
corrective: Add calibration alerts, a staging rule for customer property, and an alarm response step in the monitoring system
effectiveness: Repeat the floor walk monthly for three months

debriefText.missed: In a cleanroom, alarm logs and carrier labels hold much of the evidence.
debriefText.falseFinding: A cracked mirror and defined color coding are not quality findings.
